stem: An adult with persisting acute stroke symptoms cannot hold their head erect. What does ASSIST direct?

options.text: Stop, place the patient NBM and review when all section 1 parameters are yes
options.why: Any no in section 1 triggers this action.
The water test follows only after section 1 is passed.
This is step 5 after preceding checks.
Head control is a section 1 gate.

explanation: Any no in section 1 triggers this action.

stem: A stroke patient has facial droop before the water test. What does ASSIST direct?

options.text: Stop, place NBM and refer to speech pathology
options.why: Facial weakness or droop is a section 2 trigger.
Section 2 must be passed first.

options.text: Offer a full cup of water
options.why: The cup test is later.
Diet resumes only after screening steps pass.

explanation: Facial weakness or droop is a section 2 trigger.

stem: During the 10 mL water sip, the patient's voice quality changes. What next?

options.text: Stop, place NBM and refer to speech pathology
options.why: Voice change is a section 3 stop criterion.

options.text: Continue to the cup of water
options.why: The cup follows only if no section 3 signs occur.
The tool directs NBM at this point.

options.text: Observe only at the first meal
options.why: The patient has not passed screening.

explanation: Voice change is a section 3 stop criterion.

stem: After passing ASSIST, what is required at the first meal?

options.why: Step 5 explicitly requires first-meal observation.
The tool specifically requires it.
That is an earlier screening step.
Referral is specified for failed sections.

stem: After oral intake resumes, temperature spikes and chest condition deteriorates. What does ASSIST advise?

options.text: Place NBM and refer to speech pathology
options.why: These changes may indicate silent aspiration.
The tool directs NBM.

options.text: Repeat only the initial alertness check
options.why: The follow-up warning calls for NBM and referral.
The tool flags silent aspiration without requiring cough.

explanation: These changes may indicate silent aspiration.

stem: An initial NGT aspirate has pH greater than five. What must be ordered?

options.why: The policy requires x-ray when initial aspirate pH is greater than five.
The policy says never use auscultation.
The policy says never use litmus.
Placement must first be confirmed.

explanation: The policy requires x-ray when initial aspirate pH is greater than five.

stem: No gastric aspirate can be obtained after NGT insertion. What confirmation is required?

options.why: The policy requires an x-ray if aspirate cannot be obtained.
Auscultation must never confirm position.
Litmus cannot confirm pH.

options.text: Assume correct placement from the external length
options.why: Initial placement still requires confirmation.

explanation: The policy requires an x-ray if aspirate cannot be obtained.

stem: Before medication is given through a newly inserted NGT, which requirements apply?

options.text: Confirmed tube placement and a documented medical-officer direction to use it
options.why: Both are required before medications or feed.
Tube placement and direction to commence use are also required.
Auscultation is not a valid confirmation method.
The mark is for monitoring migration, not initial confirmation.

explanation: Both are required before medications or feed.

stem: The tube's nostril centimetre mark differs from its insertion record. What next?

options.text: Do not use it until gastric position is reconfirmed
options.why: A changed mark indicates migration and reconfirmation is required.

options.text: Continue feed if the patient does not cough
options.why: Absence of coughing does not rule out displacement.

options.text: Rely on the old x-ray alone
options.why: Placement can change after the image.

options.text: Give water through it to test patency
options.why: Use must pause until position is reconfirmed.

explanation: A changed mark indicates migration and reconfirmation is required.

stem: A patient receiving NGT feed starts coughing and aspiration is suspected. What action is specified?

options.text: Cease feeds immediately and notify the medical officer
options.why: The policy directs both actions for suspected aspiration.
This conflicts with immediate cessation.
The policy calls for cessation and notification.
Medication also requires safe tube use.

explanation: The policy directs both actions for suspected aspiration.

prompt: A trained clinician screens an adult with persisting acute stroke symptoms. Outline the ASSIST stop rules before and during water testing.
model: First check alertness for at least 20 minutes, upright sitting and head control; any no means stop, NBM and review. Any section 2 risk sign such as facial droop, slurred speech or weak cough means stop, NBM and refer to speech pathology. During a 10 mL sip or cup of water, coughing, voice change, drooling or breathing change also means stop, NBM and refer.

rubric.point: Section 1 alertness, posture and head control; any no means stop and NBM
Section 2 risk sign means NBM and speech pathology referral
Water-test cough, voice, drool or breathing change means NBM and referral

prompt: Before administering a medicine through an NGT, what placement, authorisation and medicine checks does the policy require?
model: Confirm tube position before medication, including checking for migration. A medical officer must document direction to commence tube use, and medication administration directions must be on the medication order by a pharmacist or medical officer. Confirm medication/feed compatibility, solubility and stability with pharmacists; liquid medicines are preferred to crushed medicines.

rubric.point: Placement confirmed before medicines and migration checked
Medical officer documents direction to commence use
Medication directions documented by pharmacist or medical officer
Pharmacist confirms compatibility, solubility and stability; liquids preferred
